constraints.text: Exact canvas rendering approach (Canvas 2D vs. WebGL) for achieving 60fps on target hardware
Whether save/load should be file-based on the server or localStorage in the browser
The precise commodity set and galaxy map layout for balanced gameplay
The enemy AI difficulty curve and combat balance parameters
the delivered product is synthesized and assembled as one whole that is runnable locally
an ordered smoke test performs the install step, then the start step, then reaches the running product

assumptions: Node.js (LTS) is the only runtime dependency; no Docker, no bundler, no external CDN
Browser target is Google Chrome on a 2020-era laptop
All game state is single-player; persistence via server-side file or browser localStorage, no database required
Canvas 2D is sufficient for visual effects; WebGL is optional for performance
The game is served as static assets by the Node.js server
npm test runs all unit tests; a separate smoke-test script covers the browser check
payload.candidate_scope: A Node.js HTTP server serving a single-page canvas/WebGL application. Features: galaxy of at least 8 named star systems with per-system commodity price variation, trading loop (buy low, sell high), hyperspace jumps consuming fuel with pirate-encounter risk, arcade ship-to-ship laser combat with enemy AI, ship upgrades (cargo capacity, laser, shields, fuel tank), Elite rating system tracked by profit and combat kills, save/load functionality, /healthz endpoint. Unit tests for market pricing, jump/fuel math, combat resolution, save/load. Browser smoke test verifying canvas rendering.
evidence_refs: initiative.objective: full game specification including gameplay loop, visual requirements, non-functional constraints, and testing requirements
payload.observed_context: Greenfield project (no existing code, artifacts, or notes). The repository is empty and the initiative was factory-started with a fully specified objective. Classified as XS complexity, type web-app. Runtime is Node.js serving a single-page application. Constraints: deployment excluded, local run required (npm install && npm start), human acceptance after local start in Chrome. No external CDN dependencies allowed (fully offline). The frontend is a first-class acceptance subject with specific visual requirements: parallax starfield, hyperspace jump effect, docking screen, ship HUD, commodity market, and arcade laser combat with visual effects.
payload.problem_statement: There is no single-player space trading and combat game that delivers a classic Elite-style experience playable immediately in a browser without build steps or CDN dependencies. Players who want a rich, immersive space trading experience must install native applications or rely on online services.
payload.rationale: The initiative is a well-specified, self-contained XS web-app with clear functional requirements, explicit non-functional constraints, and a bounded scope. All requirements are achievable with Node.js and vanilla browser APIs. The risks are technical implementation concerns (rendering performance, game balance), not feasibility blockers. No external dependencies, no deployment, and no multi-user concerns reduce complexity.
risks: Achieving 60fps canvas rendering with parallax starfield and combat effects on a 2020 laptop without a build step or framework
Balancing the trading economy across 8+ systems to make the buy-low/sell-high loop engaging
Implementing arcade combat with visual effects in a zero-build, no-framework frontend
Ensuring the browser smoke test is reliable across different Chrome versions
stakeholders_or_actors: Player: opens the game in Chrome, trades commodities, fights pirates, upgrades ship, pursues Elite rating
Factory operator: runs npm install && npm start locally and performs human acceptance in Chrome
unknowns: Exact canvas rendering approach (Canvas 2D vs. WebGL) for achieving 60fps on target hardware
Whether save/load should be file-based on the server or localStorage in the browser
The precise commodity set and galaxy map layout for balanced gameplay
The enemy AI difficulty curve and combat balance parameters

assumption_visibility.rationale: Six assumptions explicitly stated covering runtime (Node.js LTS only), browser target (Chrome 2020-era), game state persistence model, rendering technology, serving model, and test strategy. All are relevant and testable.

evidence_grounding.rationale: Three evidence refs ground the proposal in the initiative: the full game specification (objective), the XS web-app classification (context), and the local-run/deployment-excluded constraints. The observed_context elaborates on these with additional detail from the initiative.

problem_clarity.rationale: Problem statement clearly identifies the gap (no browser-native Elite-style game without build steps or CDN dependencies) and the target user experience. The rationale in $.rationale confirms feasibility with Node.js and vanilla browser APIs.

risk_visibility.rationale: Four risks explicitly listed targeting the main technical challenges: rendering performance, economy balancing, zero-build combat implementation, and smoke test reliability. All are implementation risks with clear mitigation paths during development.

scope_boundedness.rationale: Candidate scope enumerates specific deliverables: 8+ star systems, trading loop, hyperspace jumps, arcade combat, ship upgrades, Elite rating, save/load, /healthz endpoint, unit tests, and browser smoke test. XS complexity classification and explicit constraints (no Docker, no CDN, no deployment) bound the scope tightly.

stakeholder_coverage.rationale: Two stakeholders identified: the Player (primary user performing all game interactions) and the Factory operator (running local verification). For an XS single-player project, this covers all necessary actors.

unknowns_manageability.rationale: Four unknowns identified, all implementation design decisions (Canvas 2D vs WebGL, save/load mechanism, commodity set/layout, AI difficulty curve). None are feasibility blockers; all can be resolved during development with minimal impact on scope.

non_blocking_gaps.description: The choice between Canvas 2D and WebGL for rendering is unresolved; this is an implementation decision that does not block discovery but should be settled early in development to avoid rework.

payload.rationale: The proposal is a well-specified, self-contained XS greenfield web-app with clear functional requirements, explicit non-functional constraints, bounded scope, visible assumptions, manageable unknowns, and identified risks. All seven readiness dimensions are sufficient. No blocking gaps exist. The single non-blocking gap (rendering technology choice) is a standard implementation decision resolvable during development. The recommended outcome 'go' in $.rationale aligns with the assessment.

certificatePayload.rationale: Proposal is ready, grounded, and confident enough to proceed
